title: Operator HSM Fallback and SSO Continuity — Acceptance Criteria & Sign-off Checklist
creator: Maya Patel
description: This ticket defines the scoped acceptance criteria, test plan, and sign-off checklist for delivering operator-level HSM fallback behavior, emergency key rotation tooling, and SSO continuity guarantees in Private deployments. The goal is to ensure customers running Redwood Private / on-prem installations will have auditable key rotation procedures, deterministic SSO failover runbooks, and a validated fallback path that preserves audit continuity and data confidentiality when a managed HSM becomes unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Operator HSM fallback: When the primary HSM endpoint fails (network or device), the control plane can automatically route cryptographic operations to a pre-configured secondary HSM without requiring customer-managed config changes

Key escrow & rotation: The system provides a documented, auditable emergency rotation workflow that rotates service keys within <= 30 minutes end-to-end for the smallest private deployment topology and includes automatic re-encryption of persisted caches where applicable
SSO continuity: SAML SSO sessions continue to be honored for existing tokens during HSM fallback; new SAML assertion validation uses the secondary HSM key material without dropping active sessions

Audit log integrity: All HSM operations and emergency rotations produce tamper-evident audit events preserved in the audit log retention store and available for export to customer SIEMs within 15 minutes

KMS/HSM compatibility: Support must be demonstrated for both AWS CloudHSM and a FIPS-validated on-prem HSM vendor (test artifacts attached), and the control plane must support RSA-OAEP-256 key wrapping and ECDSA P-384 signing for service tokens

Access control: RBAC changes required to perform emergency rotation are scoped, time-limited, and require an approver from the customer org; operations are recorded to both operator and customer audit logs
Rollback: There exists a documented and tested rollback path that can restore pre-rotation keying within 60 minutes without losing write-ahead audit sequences
Canary / staged rollout: Feature is deployable with a canary toggle by customer tenant; telemetry shows no increase in auth failures beyond 0.1% during canary for 24 hours
test_plan: Integration test: Simulate primary HSM network partition; validate automatic failover to secondary HSM and that 100% of new signing requests succeed within 10 seconds of failure detection
Load test: Execute 10,000 concurrent token sign/verify operations during a forced rotation to verify latency SLOs (p50 < 50ms, p95 < 250ms) are maintained for customer tierdedicated-1

Audit verification: Trigger rotation and confirm audit events contain operation id, initiating principal, before/after key fingerprint, and are delivered to customer SIEM endpoint via syslog and stored in internal retention bucket
SSO continuity test: Create long-lived session, initiate HSM failover, and assert existing SSO sessions can authenticate against resources for at least their remaining TTL
Operator RBAC test: Attempt emergency rotation with unprivileged role and assert failure; then perform with elevated ephemeral role verified by approver flow
Chaos test: Randomly drop HSM responses during peak traffic and confirm graceful degradation metrics and that model-serving requests are not exposed to plaintext key material
signoff_checklist: PM review: Verify acceptance criteria met and all test runs attached
Security review: Security team signs off on KMS/HSM configuration, key-wrap algorithms, and audit retention policy
SRE review: SRE confirms monitoring, alerting, and runbook for failover and rollback
Design / UX: Console exposes clear toggle and status for HSM fallback and a one-click emergency rotation with confirmation modal
Legal / Compliance: Compliance confirms retention period and exportability meet enterprise customer requirements
Customer success: At least one pilot customer has validated the flow in a staging private deployment
Documentation: PRD, runbook, and customer onboarding guide published to Confluence with step-by-step rotation checklist
Release gating: Feature behind a tenant-scoped flag and enabled only after signoff
notes: Scope constrained to operator-managed HSMs for initial rollout; customer-managed BYOK escrow flow will be scoped in a follow-up ticket. We chose RSA-OAEP-256 and ECDSA P-384 for parity with common FIPS deployments. Implementation trade-offs: temporary increased latency during key rewrap is acceptable for P0 security events but must be bounded and observable.
